messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I direct a regional native-seed collection that is moving its most fragile accessions into cryogenic storage. The trustees approved the first three years, and the university's central plant supplies liquid nitrogen through a service line to our licensed room. The launch paper is nearly finished, but one clause in the service agreement concerns permanent closure of the central plant. I want the board paper to describe that clause accurately alongside the rest of the operating plan.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Map the current position first: agreement term, operating owners, funding, alarms, outage cover, and authority. Then inspect the permanent-closure clause and whether any ordinary procedure can replace the service rather than merely bridge an interruption.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The signed memorandum runs from 1 January 2027 through 31 December 2029. Central Plant Services must maintain the line, weekly deliveries, and purity records. Our collections manager owns sample preparation and inventory; the biosafety officer owns room access and quarantine; the finance director has the full three-year service fee and staffing in the approved budget. Trustees authorized 1,800 accessions, beginning with alpine grasses and wetland sedges.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: What does the room do during a missed delivery, line fault, or short plant shutdown? Those should be separated from a permanent loss of the service.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Two reserve dewars give ninety-six hours at full load. A low-level alarm calls the collections manager and Central Plant Services. For a line fault, the plant sends filled dewars within six hours. If an outage is expected to exceed seventy-two hours, the collections manager moves the highest-priority ten percent of accessions to the university medical vault under a pre-cleared transfer protocol. Quarterly drills have completed inside the timing requirement.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: That covers temporary interruption. Quote the permanent-closure language and identify who can make that decision.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Section 12 says the university Estates Council may permanently decommission the central cryogenic plant through an approved capital plan. If it does, the service obligation ends thirty days after written notice, regardless of the remaining memorandum term. Central Plant Services cannot override the council. The agreement promises cooperation on transition but no replacement plant, long-term dewar supply, or alternative storage room.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Has Estates indicated that closure is planned now? Also check whether your organization or another campus unit has authority and physical capacity to replace continuous production.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: No closure is proposed in the current capital plan, and the plant passed its five-year inspection in May. Our license allows storage and handling, not nitrogen production. The biosafety officer says an on-site generator would require a different ventilation system, pressure-vessel approval, and a new hazardous-material license. Trustees did not approve that building work, and our landlord will not permit structural changes during the lease term.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Could the medical vault or another collection take the whole load for more than an emergency bridge? Get their stated capacity and quarantine limits rather than assuming co-location means substitutability.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The medical vault director signed the emergency protocol but capped it at 180 boxes for fourteen days. The vault cannot accept untreated field material, and its clinical permit prevents routine botanical intake. The national seed center can store duplicates of sixty named accessions, not our working collection, and requires six months of testing before transfer. Neither institution has agreed to continuous service for the 1,800-accession program.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: What other launch work is still underway, and who owns those steps?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Collection consent for three nature reserves is still being signed; the field partnerships manager owns those letters and substitutes from five already-cleared reserves if a signature is late. Germination baselines are unfinished for about two hundred accessions; the seed physiologist works through weekly batches and excludes an accession from freezing until its baseline is recorded. Barcode reconciliation has a two-person check and an error queue owned by the collections manager.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Are staffing, service fees, equipment replacement, and current operating authority assigned for the approved term?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Yes. Two technicians and one collections manager are contracted through 2029. The budget includes the plant fee, alarm maintenance, replacement sensors, dewar inspection, sample packaging, and annual license fees. The finance director can move up to 40,000 euros among those operating lines, and trustees retain authority above that. The launch checklist has a named owner for every current task.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: What did the plant engineer and biosafety officer say would happen if Estates later used section 12?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The plant engineer calculated that reserve dewars plus the medical-vault allowance would protect the priority accessions for at most fourteen days. After that, the rest would warm unless moved to a licensed long-term facility. Our biosafety officer cannot approve routine botanical storage in the medical vault, and no campus unit has a continuous nitrogen line with spare room. A permanent closure would require a different host facility, a new license, or a different preservation method before the thirty-day notice expired.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Does the current memorandum require Estates to fund or approve one of those replacements, or only to cooperate?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Only to cooperate by sharing equipment records and allowing supervised removal. University counsel confirmed that the clause creates no duty to build a replacement or pay our relocation costs. The trustees accepted that term because the plant is active, inspected, and absent from the current closure plan. They did not authorize an alternative facility in advance.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Is there any routine trigger that already handles this exact event, perhaps a capital reserve or relocation authority?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The continuity appendix handles delivery delays, line faults, contamination alarms, building evacuation, and temporary plant shutdown. It authorizes the ninety-six-hour dewars, emergency vault transfer, priority ordering, and trustee notification. It explicitly says permanent decommissioning requires a new preservation plan and trustee approval because the emergency measures are time-limited. The general reserve has 75,000 euros, far below the last estimate for relocation or a generator.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: What do the most recent Estates minutes and the trustee launch approval say?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The June Estates minutes fund plant maintenance through 2028 and contain no decommissioning proposal. They also restate that any future capital plan can invoke section 12 after consultation. Our trustee resolution authorizes the collection only while continuous licensed cryogenic service is available; it directs the board to approve a replacement preservation plan if that service is permanently withdrawn.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: What remains before the first accessions move, and are those steps within the existing roles and budget?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: The biosafety officer completed the room inspection, and the alarm contractor is replacing one mislabeled sensor under warranty. The physiologist has cleared the first 140 accessions, the field partnerships manager has five reserve sites available, and the collections manager scheduled the first transfer for 12 January. All of that sits within the approved launch plan.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: Do the trustees understand that the emergency equipment is a bridge rather than continuous replacement capacity?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Yes. The signed risk note says the reserve dewars and medical-vault protocol cover short interruption only. The trustees approved launch because the central service is active and contracted, not because the collection can operate indefinitely without it. They asked for section 12 to remain on the annual risk agenda, with Estates notices sent directly to the board chair and collections manager.

messages.speaker: assistant
messages.text: I can help you prepare the annual risk-agenda entry so it preserves the current operating facts, the short-interruption procedures, the authority in section 12, and the practical limits of the emergency capacity.
